title: busbar content stream, version 2
description: The `content` export stream. Core builds every content record; an export plugin writes each line as it is given. Three closed shapes: a chunk line (`$defs.line`), the completion header written once per object (`$defs.header`), and the exchange document (`$defs.exchange`), carried as part 0. Adding, removing or retyping any member makes the schema `busbar.content.v3`. WRITER RULES: members are written in the order this file declares them, through core's one JSON line writer; every number is an integer; strings are escaped by core's JSON facade; there is no RFC 8785 canonicalization. A captured body is never parsed: utf8 bytes are embedded as a JSON string and binary bytes as base64, and `chunk.sha256` is over the decoded bytes, so a reader verifies byte-exactly whatever a SIEM does to the line. One encoded line is at most CONTENT_LINE_BYTES = 983040 bytes (960 KiB), under the 1 MiB export answer ceiling. IDEMPOTENCE: the key of a line is (object, variant, chunk.part, chunk.index); `delivery` is the core-minted delivery id the line was handed in, and a resend keeps it. CUSTODY: a delivery ACK is custody at the level the sink reports (none, accepted, durable, indexed), not durability. IDENTITY BYTE LAYOUT: be32(n) is n as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer; every member is written as be32(byte length) followed by its bytes, the domain tag included; the digest is SHA-256 over the concatenation, and the id is its first 16 bytes as 32 lowercase hex characters. `object` = SHA-256(be32(len T) T be32(len D) D be32(len J) J)[..16] with T = `busbar.content.object.v1`, D = the deployment_id bytes, J = the join id `{node_id}.{incarnation}.{unit_key}` (the correlation_id). `variant` = SHA-256(be32(len T) T, then be32(len m) m for each member in this order)[..16] with T = `busbar.content.variant.v1` and members: destination host; destination path, or bucket and prefix (userinfo and query stripped); projection; records.identity; redaction profile; event_bytes (decimal); parts; custody floor; CONTENT_LINE_BYTES (decimal). A setting at a declared secret position contributes its reference text when it is a `secret://` reference and the fixed marker `literal` otherwise; a resolved secret value is never hashed.

correlation_id.description: The request id: the node-qualified unit id node_<16 hex>.<32 hex>.<unit key>. Equals the response X-Request-Id.

object.description: The content object id; see IDENTITY BYTE LAYOUT.

variant.description: The sink variant; see IDENTITY BYTE LAYOUT.

delivery.description: The core-minted delivery id (never 0, never time-derived).

part.description: Part 0 is the exchange document; parts 1 to 255 are bodies too large to sit inline in it.

of.description: How many chunks the part has.

sha256.description: Over the decoded bytes of this chunk.

encoding.description: utf8 chunks are cut at code-point boundaries; b64 chunks at multiples of 3 raw bytes.

manifest_sha256.description: Over the object's manifest bytes, which travel as their own fragments.

of.description: How many parts the object has, part 0 included.

custody_reached.description: The lowest custody every piece of the object reached.

custody_floor.description: The sink's configured custody floor. Reached below the floor reads as custody below floor, never complete.

key_id.description: Present only when the sink also takes the identity stream.

groups.description: Present only when the sink also takes the identity stream.

body.description: The captured utf8 body as a string, never parsed.
